spec.name: cmp_a200_lowbeta_skew
spec._hypothesis: Alternative trend leg (above_200dma had the best train t60/t120) plus two mutually orthogonal defensives (low_beta vs skew_126 corr -0.09).

spec.name: cmp_mom12_cons_lowvol
spec._hypothesis: Three mutually low-correlated legs: trend (mom12), quality-of-trend (trend_consistency, corr 0.02 vs low_vol), defensive (low_vol, corr -0.41 vs mom12 = active hedge).

spec.name: cmp_mom12_lowbeta_100
spec._hypothesis: Same pair, equal weight. Weighting gradient: does more defensive weight stabilise, or just dilute the trend signal?

spec.name: cmp_mom12_lowbeta_50
spec._hypothesis: Flagship pair. low_beta is the most orthogonal factor in the library to every trend factor (train rank-corr -0.06 vs mom_12m). Moderate defensive tilt.

spec.name: cmp_mom12_lowbeta_illiq
spec._hypothesis: The two strongest NON-volatility diversifiers. illiquidity: train t60=10.1 and only 0.14 corr with mom12. CAVEAT: flat 0.25pct cost understates the true cost of an illiquidity tilt.

spec.name: cmp_mom12_sharpe_lottery
spec._hypothesis: Trend + risk-adjusted trend quality (sharpe_126, the only extended factor with positive train IC) + lottery-demand screen (corr -0.22 vs mom12).

spec.name: rb_lowbeta_25
spec._hypothesis: Weight gradient DOWN. With 0.5 and 1.0 known, 0.25 tests whether the OOS edge is a smooth function of the defensive tilt or a knife-edge fit.

spec.name: rb_lowbeta_50_hold20
spec._hypothesis: Exit-horizon test. Same selection, 20-day hold instead of 60. Tests whether the edge is a property of selection or an artifact of the long hold.

spec.name: rb_lowbeta_50_topn10
spec._hypothesis: Concentration test. If the blended RANKING carries information, a tighter cut should show MORE edge per trade, not less.

spec.name: rb_lowbeta_75
spec._hypothesis: Weight gradient fill-in between 0.5 and 1.0. A monotone/plateau shape = real; a spike at 0.5 = fit.

spec.name: rb_lowbeta_illiq_topn10
spec._hypothesis: Concentration test on the batch-1 OOS leader. Also sharpens the cost caveat: a tighter illiquidity tilt means worse real-world slippage.

spec.name: rb_mom6_lowbeta_50
spec._hypothesis: Trend-leg generalisation. Does trend+low_beta work as a PRINCIPLE, or only with the one momentum definition that happens to be the baseline?
